Purpose\n\nThe doctor/fix registry is the extension point for environment readiness. Modules register checks, fixes, and config defaults instead of adding one-off repair logic.\n\nTarget architecture has no separate `fgos setup` verb for workspace onboarding. `fgctl init` is the one-command workspace onboarding orchestrator; after activation it invokes active local `fgos init`, `fgos doctor --fix`, and `fgos doctor`. Registry Types\n\n| Registry | Function | Meaning |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Check | `registerCheck` | A named diagnostic reported by `fgos doctor`. |\n| Fix | `registerFix` | A named repair run by `fgos doctor --fix`; current legacy `fgos setup` also runs fixes while it remains implemented. |\n| Config default | `registerConfigDefault` | A default config shape merged into shared config without overwriting user values. |\n\n`event-store` registers the `eventStore` config shape `{ remote: \"origin\" }`. Config merge fills missing keys while preserving explicit remote choices; the `git-repository-config` check diagnoses obsolete exact legacy mappings on the configured remote and on historical `origin`, and the `git-publication-refspecs` fix repairs them.\n\nThe registries are independent. Doctor Contract\n\n`fgos doctor`:\n\n- runs registered checks;\n- reports individual pass/fail status as a row `{id, description, passed, message, detail?}`; `detail` is an optional JSON value that holds the facts behind the row's one-sentence `message` (for example the versions and floor behind a compatibility failure) and appears only in `fgos doctor --json`;\n- does not write files by default;\n- should tell the user what command or fix path applies when a check fails.\n\nRun coverage is checked by `observe-run-coverage`: the host's `metrics coverage`\nmust report layout rule `v2` and valid observed/skipped accounting. A candidate run\ndirectory changed in the last 60 seconds permits a bounded transient difference,\neven before a result exists; future mtimes are recent for clock skew. The host's\n`recentRuns` remains result-file based. Diagnostic paths are sample candidates,\nnot verified host omissions. An unknown coverage subcommand or a response\nwithout `layoutRule` identifies an old host positively and reports\npassed-but-degraded with an upgrade instruction; other host errors fail.\nThis check is read-only, introduces no config default, and never rewrites runs.\n\n`convention-conformance` checks the packaged naming and placement rules only\ninside an fgOS source checkout. Violations on paths already present at the\nrule cutoff pass with counts and up to three examples; a violation on a path\nintroduced after that cutoff fails the check, even while the rule posture is\n`warn`. A missing or old host pass-skips with the reason because doctor never\nreimplements the native rules. The check is read-only and has no registered\nfix or config default.\n\n\n`active-release-matches-checkout` compares a source checkout's Node payload\nworking-tree bytes with its own activated manifest, using the release builder's\nsource enumeration. It reports changed, missing and extra source files, excludes\nstaged production dependencies, and does not certify Rust host freshness.\nOutside source checkouts, without activation, with a same-checkout development\nmanifest, or in a linked worktree whose activation belongs to main, it reports\na reasoned skip. Unsafe paths and unreadable inputs fail this check rather than\nthrowing out the whole doctor run. It is read-only, with no registered fix:\n`npm run fgos:dev -- <verb>` runs working-tree code; build/stage/upgrade updates\nplain `fgos`. Diagnosis never changes the activation implicitly.\n\n\n| Check | Pass | Fail | Not applicable |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| `documentation-cutover-lease` | Repository hooks are wired, the committed main-ref sidecar is absent, released or abandoned, and no stray main token exists. | Committed sidecar is corrupt/unreadable; a token exists in main while main is not the recorded holder; applicable hook wiring is missing; or a lease is held. It diagnoses a stray main token by file presence and the recorded holder checkout, without validating a linked holder's token possession. Acquire refuses the same stray condition with `stray-main-token`; held-lease admission also refuses main callers with that residue. The check is read-only, with no registered fix, config default or automatic token cleanup. After checking committed state and the recorded holder, the owner removes residue by hand; a real holder's release restores any pre-existing main token bytes. The [lease contract](../../holder-lock/spec.md#documentation-cutover-write-lease) owns the release crash window and recovery.\n\n`fgos doctor --fix`:\n\n- runs every registered fix;\n- reports fix results;\n- then reports checks.\n\n## 4. Legacy Setup Compatibility\n\nCurrent legacy `fgos setup` is deprecated but still reachable:\n\n- wires known local support such as shell integration and hooks where applicable;\n- ensures shared config defaults are present;\n- runs every registered fix unconditionally;\n- reports changes;\n- preserves idempotency when run repeatedly.\n\nThe command registry and setup result payload expose the deprecation and workspace-onboarding path. Config Merge Contract\n\nConfig merge is fill-missing-only:\n\n- customized values are not overwritten;\n- nested object defaults fill missing keys;\n- arrays are added wholesale only when missing;\n- project config wins over global config for matching keys;\n- missing global config is not an error.\n\n## 6. Ownership Boundary\n\nDoctor/fix paths may repair environment readiness. They must not silently select a different runtime identity when a workspace activation is present. Runtime selection belongs to `fgctl` and workspace activation records.\n\n## 7.       "sourceContent": "| # | Element | Meaning | Values | Required | Default |\n|---|-------|---------|--------|----------|---------|\n| 1 | Package name | The npm package identity used for the git-based install command | `forgent` | yes | — |\n| 2 | Package version | A semantic version string tooling (e.g. packaging commands) needs to treat the package as valid | semver string | yes | `0.1.0` |\n| 3 | Distribution file allowlist | The exact set of paths shipped to anyone installing the package — everything else in the source repo is excluded | `bin`, `src`, `scripts`, `core`, `domains`, `.agents`, `README.md`, `LICENSE`, the end-user documentation subset (`docs/how-to`, `docs/explanation`, and `docs/enduser-docs-index.json`), plus `packages/convention/contracts/convention.rules.v1.json`, which installed doctor needs to interpret per-rule cutoffs without duplicating native rule data, and `packages/seat-binding/contracts/seat-binding.tier-ladder.v1.json`, the tier names the runner config loader accepts, read from the same file the Seat Binding crate embeds | yes | — |\n| 4 | CLI entry points | The commands exposed once installed | `fgos` → runs `bin/fgos.mjs`; `fgos-runner` → runs `bin/fgos-runner.mjs` (the autonomous-loop runner, see spec Runner) | yes | — |\n| 4b | Claude Code plugin skill set | `plugins/fgOS/skills/` — the Claude Code plugin's own skill bundle, distributed via the Claude Code plugin marketplace mechanism (a separate distribution channel from the npm-installed `fgos`/`fgos-runner` CLI above). Ships two layers: hand-authored CLI-wrapper skills (`cook`, `discover`, `pick`, `submit`, ...) and mirrored `fgos-*` dev-skills plus `_shared/` for plugin-only consumers. Dev-skills are authored in `core/skills/` or `domains/*/skills/`; run `npm run build:skills` in the fgOS source repo to assemble `.agents/skills/`, generate `.claude/skills/` thin wrappers and references, and mirror dev-skills/shared fragments into the plugin.       "sourceContent": "- **2026-10-12 — `fgctl init` downloads by default (RUL15 (fgctl init downloads a checksum-verified release when no source is given)).** Before this, a plain `fgctl init` in a project with no pin failed with \"`--from <source>` is required\", so a first install meant downloading the release tarball by hand. Owner decision: no source and no pin means the latest GitHub release; `FGCTL_VERSION` selects an exact tag; `FGCTL_FROM` and `--from` select a non-release build; checksum verification is mandatory; the transport is the system `curl` rather than a new HTTP crate (same behavior and override as `install.sh`, no TLS stack to carry in `fgctl`). Prior art: `fgctl init --from` (the release-asset door, kept unchanged and now equivalent to `FGCTL_FROM`), `install.sh`'s `FGCTL_VERSION`/`FGCTL_ASSET_BASE_URL`/`FGCTL_TARGET` (reused, not redefined). Same day, follow-up: the pin now records the tag, so a pinned workspace whose release is not staged on this machine downloads it instead of needing a source; only a digest-only legacy pin still needs `FGCTL_FROM`/`FGCTL_VERSION`/`--from`, because a digest names no download. Follow-up (2026-10-14): `fgctl upgrade` uses the same verified download pipeline (`--from` > `FGCTL_FROM` > `FGCTL_VERSION` > latest GitHub release) and records the downloaded tag in `.fgos/distribution.json`, so an upgraded project's pin keeps a downloadable `releaseVersion` for teammates instead of reverting to digest-only.\n- **2026-10-13 — Windows is a native release target (RUL16 (Windows is a native release target: same assets, an installer and launchers that need no POSIX shell)).** Owner decision: the level is \"native, complete\" (PowerShell and `cmd.exe`, no Git Bash, no WSL), with `tar.gz` kept as the single archive format and macOS left out of scope. Prior art, reused: the Windows CI hardening track made the Rust workspace build and the release-tree staging work on Windows (the `fgos.exe` entry, colon-free release store directory names, drive-letter-safe archive validation), and an earlier change wrote `.cmd` launchers on Windows that ran the `sh` shims through a `sh` on `PATH`; that required Git for Windows, so it is replaced by launchers that read `activation.json` themselves. Missing before: a Windows release asset, `install.ps1`, a Windows consumer proof, and any check that the launchers exist. Also in this change: the Linux asset moves from `ubuntu-latest` (binaries then needed glibc 2.39 and printed a loader warning on Ubuntu 22.04, glibc 2.35) to `ubuntu-22.04`, with a CI gate on the glibc symbol versions.\n- **2026-10-16 — fgOS has no npm runtime dependency; YAML is read through one vendored parser (RUL101 (fgOS has no npm runtime dependency; every YAML parse goes through one vendored js-yaml 5.4.3 behind src/util/yaml.mjs)).** **Superseded on 2026-10-23 by RUL108 (every YAML parse goes through the native door): the one-door rule stays, the parser behind the door is now the Rust crate, the vendored file, its hash test and the upgrade procedure below are gone; the text below is kept as history.** Before this, `yaml` was the one production dependency. An installed release carried it (the release builder stages declared production dependencies), but a checkout, linked worktree or unpacked copy without `npm install` did not, so every module importing it failed to load there, and the doctor and setup paths grew their own YAML readers and \"not evaluated\" branches to keep loading. Decision: `package.json#dependencies` stays empty; the only YAML parser is `src/util/third-party/js-yaml.mjs`, the ESM bundle from the js-yaml 5.4.3 tarball, unmodified except a header and the dropped source-map comment line, and every parse goes through `src/util/yaml.mjs` (`parseYaml(text, { filename })`: zero documents give `null`, more than one throws, `maxAliases` 100, js-yaml's default core schema). An architecture test fails on any other import of `yaml`, `js-yaml` or the third-party file. Rejected: keeping `yaml` and making doctor tolerate its absence (what the workarounds did, and the cause of the divergence); a hand-rolled parser (a second authority for what YAML means); `vendor/` or `dist/` as the location (the repository's scout-block hook refuses those path segments, so agents could not read or review the file); 5.4.2 (a block-indentation mis-parse fixed in 5.4.3) and 5.5.0 (one day old at the time). Readers that used to skip silently now report a parse failure as a named problem with file, line and column; pinned persona text that the strict parser rejects renders through a private legacy projection so older runs resume with the same text (its removal is tracked in the backlog). Evidence: commits `8ef1baf1c` (door and vendored file), `838b044e5` (call sites), `b75c01a3f` (release and dev-host staging), `6013ca389` (dependency dropped), `f96eece77`, `b7eeb4bb6` and `26b3338a7` (readers use the parser), `f705b9c8c` (doctor checks `compiled.json`); a parity run of the old parser against the door over every tracked YAML and frontmatter document found 828 documents, 0 differences, 13 rejected by both; a cold `fgos` start costs 2 to 3 ms more (97 to 99 ms for `version`, 109 to 110 ms for `dispatch decide`); the full suite ran 7850 tests with 0 failures with release binaries present; `test/util/yaml.test.mjs` pins the vendored bytes by hash.       "sourceContent": "- **RUL77 ([ĐÃ BỊ THAY phần \"each door carries one posture lane\" bởi RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed), decision 0062 — posture now comes from the Unit's `writes` plus the capability; \"an agent executor declares no `for`\" stands] posture belongs to the capability, an agent executor declares no `for`, and each door carries one posture lane; supersedes RUL76 (`execute <id> --for <capability>` with a \"must declare\" gate), 2026-10-13).** An agent executor can do any kind of work, so no `for` list describes it, and a list on one was read as the posture of every dispatch to it (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` already said a direct executor call must carry a capability anchor and never infer the minimum from `executor.for`). `resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints` reads `for` from tool executors only; on an agent executor it is inert (config still loads, so projects and worktrees that carry one keep dispatching) and `fgos doctor` names it under `executor-profile-warnings` (`executor.<id>.agent-for-inert`); the agent executors' `for` lists are gone from this repo's `.fgos/config.json` (`decide --for` routing unchanged: it reads `capabilities.<name>.prefer`). The CLI door `execute <agent>` refuses before spawning when no `--for` is given (`capability-required`, listing the writing capabilities and the read-only door); programmatic callers (Assignment, Work) pass their own capability hints and are unchanged. `execute <agent> --for <capability>` runs the invocation that capability `prefer`s for that executor, else the first plain cli invocation with no sandbox backend, instead of always the first cli invocation. That door leases no provider account, so it carries writing work only: a capability with required confinement is refused (`posture-needs-assignment`). Read-only work runs sandboxed as a Workflow unit with `writes: []` (`fgos workflow start --units`), which binds the read-only posture and leases the account (the architecture-advisory seats ran that way: `confined-bwrap`, login provisioned); `execute --contract <file> --executor <id>` keeps a named provider and leases its account but runs unconfined, read-only by instruction only (measured: `execute openai --for code:review` on the bare door ran `codex-cli-bwrap` confined and got 401 with no login; the same read through `--contract --executor openai` answered, on `cli-spawn` with `confinement: null`). A sandboxed read-only door that also keeps a named provider does not exist yet. The calling agent answers Q1 (does it write? does a provider matter?) from prose doctrine in `core/skills/_shared/capability-matching.md`, with no classifier or workflow generator. Decided after an `architecture-advisory` run (`wf-run-1791875339761-10315b91`: framing and shaping with three blind seats and a synthesizer completed; critique was blocked by a Codex trust prompt, so no reviewed synthesis exists). Not built: a soft provider hint on `decide` (`--prefer`, the synthesizer's recommendation) — naming the executor on `execute` already lets a caller pick a provider, and the hint would change `bind()`, shared with Workflow binding; revisit when a caller needs \"this provider if it can, else any\". Since 2026-10-14 (RUL88 (ad-hoc Unit prefer and persona, the one-liner), decision 0061) that hint exists on the Unit, not on `decide`: `fgos run \"<prompt>\" --provider <id>` and an ad-hoc Unit's `prefer` try the provider first and fail over into the pool, and a read-only one-liner is the sandboxed read-only door that keeps a preferred provider.\n  1. **Account lock.** One kernel mutex per provider account, machine scope, at `<stateRoot>/locks/provider-account/<provider>/<account>.lock` through holder-lock, separate from the state lock (`provider-state.lock`). A waiter waits with timers, never by blocking the event loop (panel seats share a process and may share an account); a caller that must not wait (a removal) tries once. The renewal or unlock-probe call runs through the lock (`spawnHolding`, i.e. `runBorrowed`), so a dead holder with a live call keeps the lock and a second renewal never redeems the same refresh token; the lock is released only after the call and every process it started have exited. The account directory `<runtime dir>/account-locks/<provider>/<account>/` still holds the pending copies, the scratch home and the cooldown.\n  2. **Refresh-ahead.** After the final account selection (the executor-fallback lease included) and before a confined private home is built from it, when the login has less than the window left, fgOS renews it once. The window is `max(60 minutes, probe timeout + 5 minutes)`. Only the entry of the dispatched provider counts, for the window and for \"was it renewed\" (Codex: its single entry; pi: the key equal to the provider id or starting with `<provider>-`; omp: the row `provider` likewise; a lone oauth entry of another provider is not used; zero or several matches skip the renewal as `entry-unidentified`), so an abandoned login of another provider never makes every dispatch renew, and only that entry is made due and applied. Under the account lock it applies any leftover copy first, re-reads the source, and skips for 30 minutes after a failed renewal; then it builds a scratch home under the account directory (mode 0700, the listed files only), makes only that copy look due, runs the layout's probe call on it (wrapped in coreutils `timeout --kill-after=5`, so the child ends on its own even if the runner dies and the account lock does not outlive it unbounded; the runner's own timer stays; the lazy-probe unlock call, an account locked for a dead login, is wrapped the same way), and applies the renewed entry to the real store. The real store is never made to look expired, so the owner's own CLI does not renew because of this, a failed or hung call leaves it untouched, and a scratch copy left by a dead runner is applied (if newer) by the next lock holder and then removed. Where each layout keeps its expiry: pi `auth.json` `<provider>.expires` (ms; seconds below 1e12), `type: oauth` entries only; omp `agent.db` table `auth_credentials`, `data.expires` (ms), rows `credential_type = 'oauth'` and no `disabled_cause`; Codex `auth.json`, due at the earlier of the access token's `exp` claim and `last_refresh` plus 8 days (`TOKEN_REFRESH_INTERVAL`, `should_refresh_proactively` in `codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs` of openai/codex; the same file renews at five minutes before `exp` when the token can be read). A layout that cannot be read (an API key, agy, no `node:sqlite`) is left as it was.\n  3. **Apply (compare-before-write).** Shared by refresh-ahead and write-back, always under the account lock: only an entry whose expiry is strictly later than the source's and whose refresh token differs from the source's replaces it (compared in memory, never printed; a copy that still holds the source's refresh token renewed nothing), and for a fresh renewal the new expiry must also be in the future, while a copy staged earlier (a pane's home, a pending or leftover copy) is applied even if its access token has expired since, because its refresh token is the newer one and the source's is already spent, only that entry changes (other pi providers, other omp rows and columns, other Codex fields stay as they were), a copy that cannot be read, has an unexpected shape, or has no refresh token where the source's entry has one never touches the source. A copy is deleted only when the source was read successfully and proves the copy is not newer (same refresh token, or an expiry not strictly later), or when the copy is proven malformed (corrupt JSON, or it parses to no usable entry, or it has no store file); when the source is unreadable or half-written, the entry cannot be identified at apply time, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass (`node:sqlite` unavailable, a database that will not open), the copy is kept (a fresh scratch copy moves to `pending/`) and the result is `apply-deferred`, never `applied` or `not-renewed`. An operating-system read error on a copy file (permissions, I/O) is reported as `unreadable-file` and keeps the copy (`apply-deferred`); only a store file that is not there (`missing-file`) is proven empty. pi and Codex files are replaced through a temp file and a rename, recomputed when the source changed in between; the omp store is changed by a row update in one transaction, never by replacing the file the owner's omp may hold open.\n  4. **Write-back at removal.** When a dispatch opted in, the private home's ownership marker records `credentialWriteBack` (provider, account, source home, layout, runtime dir; names and paths only). One removal function serves the driver cleanup, the finalizer of a settled dispatch and the orphan reaper: before deleting a home whose marker asks for it, a login in the home that is newer than the source's is staged under `pending/` (atomic rename) and applied under the account lock, tried once without waiting; when the lock is busy, or nothing proves the copy is not newer (the source is unreadable, its entry cannot be identified, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass, such as `node:sqlite` being unavailable: an omp store is then staged as plain files, write-ahead log included), it stays pending and the next refresh-ahead (or removal) applies it once it can be identified, even if the source still looks fresh, because the source's own refresh token may already be spent; a refresh-ahead that skips because the entry is unidentified applies the pending copies too, so the ones that have become identifiable clear. Pending copies are limited to five per login store (per account for a single-store account, per `stores/<cli>` for a per-CLI one), but only redundant ones are ever dropped: after the pending copies were applied, under the account lock, a copy whose logins are identical to another pending copy's (compared in memory by entry key, refresh token and expiry, or by the bytes of the store files and of a non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal when a copy cannot be parsed; never printed) is dropped, oldest first, while the account is over the limit, and the newest of each identical group stays; a drop writes one stderr line `credential-pending-dropped` with a count only. A copy that cannot be shown redundant, or obsolete by the source, is never dropped to make room, so an account can stay over the limit, and the doctor check reports it. A staged copy and the pending directory are synced to disk before the home goes. A copy a probe left half-written (pi rewrites its store in place; omp commits row updates in a database transaction) is kept under `torn/` for hand recovery, never applied or dropped automatically, and reported by the doctor check at any age. This covers the probe's scratch copy only: a scratch home a dead runner left, and a pane home whose store was cut off, are still removed when their JSON cannot be read. A pane home whose store files are byte for byte the source's, with no non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal on either side (a login renewed before a checkpoint sits only there; a zero-byte or missing one counts as none, the shared-memory index counts for nothing, and one that cannot be read, other than as missing, is never taken for none), renewed nothing and is not staged, parsable or not. If staging itself fails, the private home and its marker are kept (the removal reports failure, one stderr line with a fixed code and no path or value) so a later removal, the reaper's included, retries; only a copy proven malformed, or one the source was read to prove not newer, lets the home go. Each failed attempt is counted in the marker (`credentialKept`: attempts, first time, time of the last counted attempt; failures less than 15 minutes after the last counted one are not counted again, so a transient fault does not use the budget up); the marker is rewritten through a temp file and a rename, and a marker that is present but unreadable stops the removal. After five attempts the home is held: no further removal attempt and no deletion by age, however old. A held home is re-checked, under the account lock, when that account is next renewed (the temp roots searched are the same as doctor's: the default one plus each registered backend's own `tempRoot`; a home under a backend's separate `privateHomeRoot` is in none of them, so no check, repair, reaper or renewal sees it, and it is never deleted either) and by `fgos doctor --fix`, and only a home of the lock's own runtime directory: it is removed only when the source is readable and proves its login is not newer, or when that login can now be staged beside the source (and is applied); otherwise it stays held. A marker file that is no recognisable marker at all (not JSON, not an object, no contract name) stops any removal of its home. The finalizer compares the ownership marker's digest without `credentialKept` (a failed driver cleanup adds it after the digest was taken) and carries on with the dispatch's other resources past a home that cannot go (the dispatch is recorded as retained, with the home's reason).         "content": "- **RUL77 ([ĐÃ BỊ THAY phần \"each door carries one posture lane\" bởi RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed), decision 0062 — posture now comes from the Unit's `writes` plus the capability; \"an agent executor declares no `for`\" stands] posture belongs to the capability, an agent executor declares no `for`, and each door carries one posture lane; supersedes RUL76 (`execute <id> --for <capability>` with a \"must declare\" gate), 2026-10-13).** An agent executor can do any kind of work, so no `for` list describes it, and a list on one was read as the posture of every dispatch to it (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` already said a direct executor call must carry a capability anchor and never infer the minimum from `executor.for`). `resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints` reads `for` from tool executors only; on an agent executor it is inert (config still loads, so projects and worktrees that carry one keep dispatching) and `fgos doctor` names it under `executor-profile-warnings` (`executor.<id>.agent-for-inert`); the agent executors' `for` lists are gone from this repo's `.fgos/config.json` (`decide --for` routing unchanged: it reads `capabilities.<name>.prefer`). The CLI door `execute <agent>` refuses before spawning when no `--for` is given (`capability-required`, listing the writing capabilities and the read-only door); programmatic callers (Assignment, Work) pass their own capability hints and are unchanged. `execute <agent> --for <capability>` runs the invocation that capability `prefer`s for that executor, else the first plain cli invocation with no sandbox backend, instead of always the first cli invocation. That door leases no provider account, so it carries writing work only: a capability with required confinement is refused (`posture-needs-assignment`). Read-only work runs sandboxed as a Workflow unit with `writes: []` (`fgos workflow start --units`), which binds the read-only posture and leases the account (the architecture-advisory seats ran that way: `confined-bwrap`, login provisioned); `execute --contract <file> --executor <id>` keeps a named provider and leases its account but runs unconfined, read-only by instruction only (measured: `execute openai --for code:review` on the bare door ran `codex-cli-bwrap` confined and got 401 with no login; the same read through `--contract --executor openai` answered, on `cli-spawn` with `confinement: null`). A sandboxed read-only door that also keeps a named provider does not exist yet. The calling agent answers Q1 (does it write? does a provider matter?) from prose doctrine in `core/skills/_shared/capability-matching.md`, with no classifier or workflow generator. Decided after an `architecture-advisory` run (`wf-run-1791875339761-10315b91`: framing and shaping with three blind seats and a synthesizer completed; critique was blocked by a Codex trust prompt, so no reviewed synthesis exists). Not built: a soft provider hint on `decide` (`--prefer`, the synthesizer's recommendation) — naming the executor on `execute` already lets a caller pick a provider, and the hint would change `bind()`, shared with Workflow binding; revisit when a caller needs \"this provider if it can, else any\". Since 2026-10-14 (RUL88 (ad-hoc Unit prefer and persona, the one-liner), decision 0061) that hint exists on the Unit, not on `decide`: `fgos run \"<prompt>\" --provider <id>` and an ad-hoc Unit's `prefer` try the provider first and fail over into the pool, and a read-only one-liner is the sandboxed read-only door that keeps a preferred provider.\n  1. **Account lock.** One kernel mutex per provider account, machine scope, at `<stateRoot>/locks/provider-account/<provider>/<account>.lock` through holder-lock, separate from the state lock (`provider-state.lock`). A waiter waits with timers, never by blocking the event loop (panel seats share a process and may share an account); a caller that must not wait (a removal) tries once. The renewal or unlock-probe call runs through the lock (`spawnHolding`, i.e. `runBorrowed`), so a dead holder with a live call keeps the lock and a second renewal never redeems the same refresh token; the lock is released only after the call and every process it started have exited. The account directory `<runtime dir>/account-locks/<provider>/<account>/` still holds the pending copies, the scratch home and the cooldown.\n  2. **Refresh-ahead.** After the final account selection (the executor-fallback lease included) and before a confined private home is built from it, when the login has less than the window left, fgOS renews it once. The window is `max(60 minutes, probe timeout + 5 minutes)`. Only the entry of the dispatched provider counts, for the window and for \"was it renewed\" (Codex: its single entry; pi: the key equal to the provider id or starting with `<provider>-`; omp: the row `provider` likewise; a lone oauth entry of another provider is not used; zero or several matches skip the renewal as `entry-unidentified`), so an abandoned login of another provider never makes every dispatch renew, and only that entry is made due and applied. Under the account lock it applies any leftover copy first, re-reads the source, and skips for 30 minutes after a failed renewal; then it builds a scratch home under the account directory (mode 0700, the listed files only), makes only that copy look due, runs the layout's probe call on it (wrapped in coreutils `timeout --kill-after=5`, so the child ends on its own even if the runner dies and the account lock does not outlive it unbounded; the runner's own timer stays; the lazy-probe unlock call, an account locked for a dead login, is wrapped the same way), and applies the renewed entry to the real store. The real store is never made to look expired, so the owner's own CLI does not renew because of this, a failed or hung call leaves it untouched, and a scratch copy left by a dead runner is applied (if newer) by the next lock holder and then removed. Where each layout keeps its expiry: pi `auth.json` `<provider>.expires` (ms; seconds below 1e12), `type: oauth` entries only; omp `agent.db` table `auth_credentials`, `data.expires` (ms), rows `credential_type = 'oauth'` and no `disabled_cause`; Codex `auth.json`, due at the earlier of the access token's `exp` claim and `last_refresh` plus 8 days (`TOKEN_REFRESH_INTERVAL`, `should_refresh_proactively` in `codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs` of openai/codex; the same file renews at five minutes before `exp` when the token can be read). A layout that cannot be read (an API key, agy, no `node:sqlite`) is left as it was.\n  3. **Apply (compare-before-write).** Shared by refresh-ahead and write-back, always under the account lock: only an entry whose expiry is strictly later than the source's and whose refresh token differs from the source's replaces it (compared in memory, never printed; a copy that still holds the source's refresh token renewed nothing), and for a fresh renewal the new expiry must also be in the future, while a copy staged earlier (a pane's home, a pending or leftover copy) is applied even if its access token has expired since, because its refresh token is the newer one and the source's is already spent, only that entry changes (other pi providers, other omp rows and columns, other Codex fields stay as they were), a copy that cannot be read, has an unexpected shape, or has no refresh token where the source's entry has one never touches the source. A copy is deleted only when the source was read successfully and proves the copy is not newer (same refresh token, or an expiry not strictly later), or when the copy is proven malformed (corrupt JSON, or it parses to no usable entry, or it has no store file); when the source is unreadable or half-written, the entry cannot be identified at apply time, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass (`node:sqlite` unavailable, a database that will not open), the copy is kept (a fresh scratch copy moves to `pending/`) and the result is `apply-deferred`, never `applied` or `not-renewed`. An operating-system read error on a copy file (permissions, I/O) is reported as `unreadable-file` and keeps the copy (`apply-deferred`); only a store file that is not there (`missing-file`) is proven empty. pi and Codex files are replaced through a temp file and a rename, recomputed when the source changed in between; the omp store is changed by a row update in one transaction, never by replacing the file the owner's omp may hold open.\n  4. **Write-back at removal.** When a dispatch opted in, the private home's ownership marker records `credentialWriteBack` (provider, account, source home, layout, runtime dir; names and paths only). One removal function serves the driver cleanup, the finalizer of a settled dispatch and the orphan reaper: before deleting a home whose marker asks for it, a login in the home that is newer than the source's is staged under `pending/` (atomic rename) and applied under the account lock, tried once without waiting; when the lock is busy, or nothing proves the copy is not newer (the source is unreadable, its entry cannot be identified, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass, such as `node:sqlite` being unavailable: an omp store is then staged as plain files, write-ahead log included), it stays pending and the next refresh-ahead (or removal) applies it once it can be identified, even if the source still looks fresh, because the source's own refresh token may already be spent; a refresh-ahead that skips because the entry is unidentified applies the pending copies too, so the ones that have become identifiable clear. Pending copies are limited to five per login store (per account for a single-store account, per `stores/<cli>` for a per-CLI one), but only redundant ones are ever dropped: after the pending copies were applied, under the account lock, a copy whose logins are identical to another pending copy's (compared in memory by entry key, refresh token and expiry, or by the bytes of the store files and of a non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal when a copy cannot be parsed; never printed) is dropped, oldest first, while the account is over the limit, and the newest of each identical group stays; a drop writes one stderr line `credential-pending-dropped` with a count only. A copy that cannot be shown redundant, or obsolete by the source, is never dropped to make room, so an account can stay over the limit, and the doctor check reports it. A staged copy and the pending directory are synced to disk before the home goes. A copy a probe left half-written (pi rewrites its store in place; omp commits row updates in a database transaction) is kept under `torn/` for hand recovery, never applied or dropped automatically, and reported by the doctor check at any age. This covers the probe's scratch copy only: a scratch home a dead runner left, and a pane home whose store was cut off, are still removed when their JSON cannot be read. A pane home whose store files are byte for byte the source's, with no non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal on either side (a login renewed before a checkpoint sits only there; a zero-byte or missing one counts as none, the shared-memory index counts for nothing, and one that cannot be read, other than as missing, is never taken for none), renewed nothing and is not staged, parsable or not. If staging itself fails, the private home and its marker are kept (the removal reports failure, one stderr line with a fixed code and no path or value) so a later removal, the reaper's included, retries; only a copy proven malformed, or one the source was read to prove not newer, lets the home go. Each failed attempt is counted in the marker (`credentialKept`: attempts, first time, time of the last counted attempt; failures less than 15 minutes after the last counted one are not counted again, so a transient fault does not use the budget up); the marker is rewritten through a temp file and a rename, and a marker that is present but unreadable stops the removal. After five attempts the home is held: no further removal attempt and no deletion by age, however old. A held home is re-checked, under the account lock, when that account is next renewed (the temp roots searched are the same as doctor's: the default one plus each registered backend's own `tempRoot`; a home under a backend's separate `privateHomeRoot` is in none of them, so no check, repair, reaper or renewal sees it, and it is never deleted either) and by `fgos doctor --fix`, and only a home of the lock's own runtime directory: it is removed only when the source is readable and proves its login is not newer, or when that login can now be staged beside the source (and is applied); otherwise it stays held. A marker file that is no recognisable marker at all (not JSON, not an object, no contract name) stops any removal of its home. The finalizer compares the ownership marker's digest without `credentialKept` (a failed driver cleanup adds it after the digest was taken) and carries on with the dispatch's other resources past a home that cannot go (the dispatch is recorded as retained, with the home's reason). The doctor check `credential-copies-retained` reports, by provider and account, held homes (a failure, naming the home directory), homes still being retried and pending or scratch copies older than a day (warnings), with counts, ages and never a value; the check deletes nothing. Any other write-back problem is reported on stderr by a fixed code and never stops the removal.\n  5. **Known exposure.** Refresh-ahead can spend the refresh token that a pane started just outside the window still holds: that pane's own renewal is then refused, no worse than before this rule, and write-back cannot rescue it because its renewal failed. A run that copied the login with more than the window left and runs longer than that remainder is the case.\n  6. **No value in any output.** Results, events, markers, cooldown and lock records, stderr and reports carry fixed codes (`unreadable-json`, `unexpected-shape`, `sqlite-unavailable`, ...) and fingerprints at most, never a token or a parser message (which quotes nearby input).\n- **RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store, 2026-10-13).** A herdr pane with a private home carries the login of the account the capacity layer leased (RUL65b), but the folder-trust seed (`seedWorkspaceTrust`, `trustStorePaths` in `src/runner/dispatch/herdr-round.mjs`) derived the trust decision from the store of the account the invocation's static env names (`codex-herdr-fgovn`: `CODEX_HOME=${HOME}/.codex-fgovn`). When the two accounts differ and the static one was never asked about the repo, the seed refused (`untrusted-root`) and Codex stopped at \"Trust this folder?\" (measured 2026-10-13 14:24, run `unit-run-1791876207053-efe6686b/reviewer/1/runs/01`: the leased `tetcu72` trusts `/home/vantt/projects/forgentX`, `~/.codex-fgovn/config.toml` did not; reproduced read-only with a scratch static home: the main-branch code blocked on herdr rule `trust_directory`, the fixed code settled confined). Now the leased credential source travels with the dispatch (`executeThroughConfinement` adapter option `trustAccountSource` -> herdr-spawn adapter -> the round), and for a round with its own private home the decision is read from that account's store: a `codex-home` source's `config.toml`, a `home-files` source's agy settings. A declared `trustStore.path` still wins; a round without a private home still reads the invocation's home, because that is what its CLI reads. Codex hook trust, seeded from the same root, follows. The \"trust vanishing\" of 2026-10-07 (another Codex session rewriting an account `config.toml`) is a separate cause this does not remove: it still bites when the leased account's own entry is lost. Not proven: whether Codex 0.160 honours trust given to an ancestor directory (`/home/vantt/projects`); the seed still requires the repo root itself.\n- **RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment, diagnostic only, 2026-10-13).** A dispatch failure on one CLI does not say whether the account (dead login, quota) or the CLI (trust prompt, sandbox, version bug) is at fault. `fgos dispatch probe-account --provider <p> --account <a> [--executor <id>] [--invocation <id,...>] [--timeout-ms <ms>]` (`src/runner/dispatch/provider-account-probe.mjs`) starts every invocation that runs as the account at once through the Assignment door a Workflow unit uses (read-only posture binding, invocation pinned by `cliOverride`, inventory narrowed to the one account so the lease cannot pick another and a quarantine still refuses, RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home) renewal opt-in), with a trivial prompt, and reports per CLI an outcome class (`ok`, `blocked-trust-prompt`, `auth`, `quota`, `sandbox`, `timeout`, `other`), the evidence line, the assignment, run directory and pane, plus a verdict (`healthy`; `account-fault` when every CLI failed with `auth`/`quota`; `cli-fault` when one answered; `mixed`; `no-confined-cli` when no probed invocation declares a sandbox). The verdict reads only the rows whose invocation declares its own sandbox (`confined: true`, each row's `inVerdict`): the read-only posture makes the door confine every round (`resolvePosture` returns a required `host-write-denied` requirement), and an invocation that declares no sandbox binds no private home either, so its CLI meets its own login directory (`CODEX_HOME`, `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`) mounted read-only and stops on `EROFS` before it answers. That row is still run and reported (outcome `sandbox`, truthfully: a read-only dispatch pinned to that invocation fails the same way), but it says nothing about the account or the CLI (2026-10-13: tetcu72, fgovn and tetnu answered on every sandboxed invocation while `pi-cli-<account>` and `codex-cli-bypass-fgovn` died on `EROFS` under `local-bwrap-v1`, and the verdict read `cli-fault`). An invocation runs as the account when it is confined with a private home whose CLI the account's credential layout logs in (`lease`), when its credential env names the account home (`env`), or when its id ends with `-<account>` (`name`, the config's `<bin>-<mode>-<account>` convention). It closes the panes the rounds left open and removes the private homes kept for them; it picks and schedules nothing. First real run (openai/tetcu72): both Codex invocations `ok` (cli-spawn under bwrap and the herdr pane), both pi invocations `sandbox` (`EROFS` on `~/.pi/accounts/openai-tetcu72/settings.json.lock`: under the read-only posture pi cannot write its own account directory, which it does before answering; outside confinement the same pi account answered), verdict `cli-fault`.\n- **RUL80 (an account is chosen first, then a CLI: one login store per CLI, quota and locks per account, 2026-10-13).** One provider account may be used through several CLIs (Codex, pi, omp), and each CLI keeps its own login store, so an account declared with a single `credentialSource` gave every confined CLI the one store (openai `tetcu72` declared its Codex home, so its confined pi invocations got a Codex login and pi failed on its own directory, RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment)). An account in the machine-global inventory now declares exactly one of `credentialSource` (one store, used for every CLI, unchanged; other projects use it) or `credentialSources` (`{ <store key>: <source> }`, the key is the store key an invocation declares in `credentialStore.use` (RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)): `codex`, `pi`, `omp`, `agy`; each source has the same `kind`/`home`/`files` shape). Every reader takes the store of the CLI actually dispatched: the confinement request (`buildConfinementRequest`) resolves `providerCapacity.credentialSource` from the invocation's store key, so private-home provisioning, the write-back marker and the folder-trust seed (RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store)) see that store, and a CLI the leased account has no store for is refused before the worker starts (`credential-provisioning`). The lease does not know the invocation unless it is pinned (`cliOverride.preferInvocation`, as Workflow units and the account probe pin it): a pinned lease only picks an account that has a store for the pinned CLI (`provider-capacity.no-account-for-cli` when none has); an unpinned lease picks among all accounts as before. *(Superseded by RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine per pool): the lease now receives the CLI from the launched invocation's declared login store, pinned or not, so an account with no store for that CLI is never leased.)* Refresh-ahead (RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home)) runs before the invocation is settled, so for a per-CLI account it renews the store of each CLI the executor may still launch (the pinned one only, when pinned); the lazy unlock probe (RUL74 (an account locked for a dead login unlocks itself after one real call)) calls through the store of the first such CLI. Renewal copies of a per-CLI store wait under `account-locks/<provider>/<account>/stores/<cli>/` (`pending/`, scratch homes, cooldown), never beside another store's copies, and the marker records the store; the account lock stays one per account, and `credential-copies-retained` reads both places. A copy left where the account's current layout does not read (the account directory after the account moved to one store per CLI, `stores/<cli>` after it went back to one store or dropped that CLI, or an account the inventory no longer lists) is never applied, moved to the new layout or dropped: when the machine-global inventory was read, the check fails on it at any age (a torn copy and an over-limit pending directory there included) and names that directory for hand recovery; when the global config cannot be read or is refused by the validator, the check fails instead, names the reason (an error class and the config path, never the parser's own text), lists every retained copy at any age and promises nothing about a dispatch, since a dispatch could not run on that config either. Quota, leases, quarantine and rotation stay per account: no account is split into pseudo-accounts per CLI. The account probe (RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment)) leases an account into each confined CLI it has a store for. `confined-pane-accounts` in `fgos doctor` checks each confined invocation that reads a store against the store it names (RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)). An fgos release from before this rule refuses an inventory that uses `credentialSources` (unknown account key), so the inventory is changed only after the release that reads it is active. The same store directory also holds `torn/` (a login store a probe left half-written, kept for hand recovery and never applied or dropped), and a crash during staging can leave `pending/.tmp-<pid>-<id>`: `credential-copies-retained` reports it once its writer process is gone and it has not changed for ten minutes, and `fgos doctor --fix` removes one only after claiming it by rename (so a writer that is still running loses its own rename and keeps its home) and only when it is empty, has the same files as a copy the store keeps in `pending/` or `torn/` (the shared-memory index aside), or, under the account lock, the source login of the account shows it is no newer or it is malformed; never by age, and any other stays for hand recovery. A staging in a store the account's layout no longer reads is reported once with the stranded copies and is never touched. The doctor check and fix also read the `tempRoot` and `privateHomeRoot` a registered backend declares (absolute, without duplicates) for kept homes; the orphan reaper, the dispatch retries and the root-mode tightening stay on the default temp root, since they delete and re-mode what they find. Nothing retries a kept home under a scan-only root by itself, so doctor treats one as held at once (a failure naming the path) and `--fix` settles it by the same rule as any held home. Not built: per-CLI stores for an unconfined invocation, which keeps naming its store through its own env.\n  - Phần chọn ghế của rule này bị D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) thay một phần, 2026-10-20: authority đích là [seat-binding.md](../../../seat-binding/spec.md); code đổi cùng plan của nó. Chữ rule ở trên không sửa tại chỗ.\n- **RUL82 (`RunResult.confinement` names the backend that ran, 2026-10-14).** The field was always `null`: settlement compared the requested mode with `'confined'`, a mode that does not exist (`CONFINEMENT_MODES` is `required`/`preferred`/`unconfined`), and the Assignment's confinement requirement never reached settlement. It now comes from `ranConfinementBackend` (`settlement.mjs`): the prepared-invocation record the Confinement Authority published for the launch (`protected/prepared-invocation/<launchCommandId>.json`, backend type, `none` → `null`), else the attestation the dispatch returned with outcome `enforced`. A requested posture is never evidence of what ran. The field is backend provenance only and attributes no write to the run.\n- **RUL83 (a snapshot names what changed, never who: correlated write evidence is a warning, 2026-10-14).** Four paths refused a round on a before/after snapshot alone: the CLI/Work doors' `strayWriteError` (repo root dirty paths outside the workspace, 819a61e55), settlement's `read-only-mutation` (`computeChangedFiles` includes every file of every commit that moved the cwd's HEAD during the run), the normalizer's fallback `mutated-dirty-before-files`/`read-only-mutation`, and the read-back evidence floor (`deriveEvidenceFloor`). All four were measured refusing work another session caused: a Doer round (2026-10-14 09:30-10:01) for three reports written into main; two critique reviewers of one panel for files the caller and other lanes wrote; a read-only framing seat (`wf-run-1791954133905-844903ed`) for five reports another session committed to main at 12:03:38. Settlement now decides through one policy, `evaluateAttributionPolicy` (`evidence-attribution.mjs`, previously without a production caller): post-run changes and changed pre-existing dirt are `correlated`, reported in `RunResult.warnings` (`read-only-mutation-correlated`, `mutated-dirty-before-correlated`, `outside-write-scope-correlated`: code, level, basis, paths), and the run is accepted; only `proven` writes (a run-bound written-path observer's attestation within its coverage) are refused (`read-only-mutation`, `outside-write-scope`). No such observer exists yet; building one is its own decision. The CLI/Work doors put `stray-write-correlated` (with `repoRoot` and paths) on the dispatch result's `warnings` and print it on stderr. Accepted residual risk: a worker that really writes into the main checkout, the agy incident, is now flagged rather than refused. `rollbackReadOnlyMutations` (a `git reset --soft` plus deletion in the run's cwd, never called) is removed: run against a shared checkout it would undo another session's commit. Decided by the one-door council (`plans/261014-1033-dispatch-operator-improvements/reports/council-261014-1231-dispatch-one-door-conclusion.md`, step 2, finding RT2-3). Work, the consumer, still does not advance on such a result: a read-only result carrying `read-only-mutation-correlated` or `mutated-dirty-before-correlated` (or, read back from disk, a non-empty `evidence.changedFiles`/`mutatedDirtyBeforeFiles`, since stored warnings are as writable as any other field) stops with its own reason `assignment-<operation>-correlated-mutation` (at planning: `validation-correlated-mutation-do-not-advance-work`), never folded into no-evidence; a round that failed on its own terms (non-zero exit, a timeout settles as 124; a policy refusal, a proven write among them; a provider, resource or contract failure) keeps `assignment-<operation>-failed`. A stored result read back without its assignment takes its mutation from its operation and recorded `role`, never from a field of its own. The executor CLI door's `stray-write-correlated` (the main checkout changed while an isolated round ran) is kept in `result.json` beside settlement's own warnings but does not stop Work: it cannot have changed the round's own checkout, and on a busy main checkout nearly every round would carry it. Dispatch keeps the warning and does not refuse the round (`src/runner/operation-choice.mjs` `hasReadOnlyCorrelatedMutation`; Lead decision B in `plans/261014-1400-two-doors-one-rununit/phase-00-land-finished-lanes.md`).\n- **RUL84 (one write-scope matcher: a Unit's `writes` has one spelling, and every \"is this path in scope\" question goes through `matchesWriteScope`, 2026-10-14; decision 0060).** `writes` entries are normalized once (`./`, `//`, a trailing `/` and `/.` collapse; duplicates dropped, first-seen order kept) and refused when they are `.`, empty, absolute, hold a `..` segment, a `\\` or NUL, start with `:` (git pathspec magic) or glue `**` to other characters. Only `*` (inside one segment) and `**` (a whole segment, zero or more segments) are globs; every other character, `[ ] { } ! ?` included, is literal. A plain entry covers the path and everything beneath it; a glob entry must match the whole path; nothing under `.fgos/` is ever in scope, not even for `**`. One leaf module, `src/runner/dispatch/write-scope.mjs` (`canonicalizeWrites`, `expandGenerated`, `matchesWriteScope`, `partitionPaths`), answers for the runner commit, settlement coverage and the Workflow out-of-scope check; git never interprets a scope. Workflow definitions use the same normalizer, and a `writes` that is not an array (YAML `writes:` left empty is `null`) is refused instead of read as `[]`. Config key `runner.generatedPaths: [{ from, also }]` (default `[]`, doctor `runner-generated-paths`): a Unit whose `writes` overlaps a generated source (`from`, e.g. `core/skills/**`) also gets that source's render trees (`also`). The widened scope is stored once in `unit.json#writeScope` when the unit run is created, never recomputed on resume, and is the `writes` of every assignment of that Unit.\n- **RUL85 (the runner commits only the Unit's write scope, and refuses to start a writing Unit over a foreign staged index, 2026-10-14; decision 0060, replaces items 1-2 of 0052).** After a passing round the runner stages and commits only the changed paths inside `writeScope`; a path outside it is never committed, and one the agent changed is reported in `commit.outOfScope`. The pin selects the candidate of the chosen family whose pool matches; otherwise the seat binds unpinned and `provenance.account.skipped` names why (`account-pin-other-pool`, `account-pin-no-inventory`, `account-pin-unsupported`); an unknown account of the seat's own pool refuses `account-pin-unknown` and a disabled one `account-pin-disabled`. `binding.account` is `{ pool, id }`. `fgos workflow start --account` takes the same form and checks it against the pool's inventory at start. **Reversal triggers.** (3) Declared order goes back to least-lease ranking if one account keeps hitting its quota window while others sit idle (watch: `fgos dispatch inspect --provider-capacity` shows `openLeases` and quarantines per account).
